newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia LUKoil sees 1997 profit growth falling.
newsitem.headline: Russia LUKoil sees 1997 profit growth falling.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil 0#LKOH.RUO said on Friday it saw 1997 profits growing more slowly than in previous years as a result of planned investment.

"We don't think that our revenues will considerably grow because we have very serious investment plans...we will increase our profit next year but it will not be as considerable as in 1996 and 1995," Pyotr Neyev, a spokesman for LUKoil, said.
"We think that 1997 could be called the investment year for LUKoil."
Asked when LUKoil profits could improve based on the investment, Neyev said it was possible in 1998.
LUKoil posted 1996 net profits earlier this month of 3.87 trillion roubles up from 2.40 trillion roubles in 1995.
The numbers were prepared according to Russian accounting standards, which differ significantly from those normally operating in the West.
LUKoil has not yet published figures to international standards but has appointed auditing firm KPMG to prepare such figures.
Neyev did not specify what the plans were or how much the investment would be worth.
But by Russian oil-company standards, LUKoil has a relatively agressive exploration programme both at home and abroad.
